steps.say: A nerve transfer is shortening the race for regrowing axons. High proximal injuries are being converted into low distal joins placed beside the neuromuscular junctions. Millimetres of regrowth are replacing decimetres of delay, and muscles are seeing axons before their motor endplates are dying.
steps.tx: **Nerve transfers** (rerouting expendable donor fascicles into a denervated target near its muscle) convert high proximal nerve injuries into low distal nerve **coaptations** (surgical joins) close to the target **neuromuscular junctions** (the nerve to muscle synapses), avoiding prolonged regenerative delays. Proximity beats graft length whenever the window is closing.

vis.caption: Radial wrist drop, ulnar claw hand, and median thenar wasting: the palsies that transfers correct. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Wrist and finger extension are being rebuilt from median nerve donors in radial palsy. Pronator teres branches are joining the ECRB while FDS fascicles are joining the posterior interosseous nerve. Two median expendables are restoring the whole radial territory.
steps.tx: In high **radial nerve palsy** (wrist drop with lost finger extension), median nerve motor branches are transferred directly: **pronator teres** **PT** (the forearm rotator) and **FDS** fascicles (superficialis finger flexor slips) go to **ECRB** (the wrist extensor) and the **PIN** (posterior interosseous nerve driving finger extension), restoring wrist plus finger extension together.

steps.say: Finger flexion is returning through a borrowed radial branch in median palsy. The expendable extensor carpi radialis brevis branch is being transferred to the anterior interosseous nerve. The reinnervated AIN is driving flexion again, and pinch is returning.
steps.tx: In high **median nerve palsy** (lost thumb opposition and finger flexion), expendable branches of the radial nerve, the extensor carpi radialis brevis **ECRB**, are transferred to the **anterior interosseous nerve** **AIN** (the deep median branch) to restore finger flexion. One expendable wrist extensor buys back the whole flexor cascade.

steps.say: Hand intrinsics are waking through a tiny forearm donor in ulnar palsy. The distal anterior interosseous branch to pronator quadratus is being transferred onto the ulnar deep motor branch. Intrinsic return is arriving months sooner than any elbow-level graft could manage.
steps.tx: In **ulnar nerve** intrinsic palsy (clawed fingers with lost pinch), the distal **anterior interosseous nerve** **AIN** branch to **pronator quadratus** (the deep square forearm rotator) transfers to the ulnar **deep motor branch** (the intrinsic supply), preserving hand intrinsics. A centimetre-scale donor rescues the whole intrinsic apparatus.

Classic **Boyes** or **Brand** **tendon transfer** (one-stage rerouting for unrecoverable radial palsy) for **radial nerve palsy** transfers **pronator teres** **PT** to **ECRB** for wrist extension, **FCU** or **FDS** to **EDC** (finger extensors) for finger extension, and **PL** (palmaris longus) to **EPL** (thumb extensor) for thumb extension. Three donors restore the full radial cascade in one sitting.
steps.say: Three borrowed tendons are restoring the whole radial cascade in one operation. Pronator teres is moving to ECRB for the wrist, FCU or FDS is moving to the finger extensors, and palmaris longus is moving to the thumb extensor. Boyes and Brand planning is making the drop hand work again.

points: FCU or FDS to finger extensors
right.title: Completing the set

steps.say: Thumb opposition is being rebuilt from borrowed motors. Flexor digitorum superficialis, the Huber abductor digiti minimi, or extensor indicis proprius is being rerouted to drag the thumb into opposition. Low median palsy is stopping being a pinchless hand.
steps.tx: **Opponensplasty** (tendon rerouting restoring thumb opposition) for low median nerve palsy restores thumb opposition by transferring **flexor digitorum superficialis** **FDS** (a finger flexor), the **Huber** transfer (**abductor digiti minimi**, the little-finger abductor), or **extensor indicis proprius** **EIP** (the independent index extensor). Each donor is redirected to pull the thumb across the palm.

steps.say: The claw is showing unbalanced joints, and dynamic tethers are rebalancing them. Metacarpophalangeal hyperextension with interphalangeal flexion is defining low ulnar clawing. Stiles-Bunnell and Zancolli lasso transfers are recreating the intrinsic pull and are straightening the cascade.
steps.tx: **Claw hand** deformity (intrinsic minus posture) in low ulnar nerve palsy causes **MCP** joint hyperextension and **IP** joint flexion, corrected dynamically via **Stiles-Bunnell** or **Zancolli lasso** transfers (flexor slips looped to mimic intrinsic action). The lasso tethers restore the balance that dead intrinsics no longer provide.

vis.alt: Forearm dissection showing the anterior interosseous nerve supplying deep flexors with a pinch test inset.
vis.caption: The anterior interosseous nerve drives deep flexion; its branches are the currency of median and ulnar transfers. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Transfers are succeeding only on prepared hands. Joints are staying supple with full passive range, donors are grading four or five in strength, and synergic patterns are easing retraining. A stiff joint or a weak donor is guaranteeing failure before the first stitch.
steps.tx: **Tendon transfer prerequisites** (the non-negotiable entry checks for success) include supple joints with full passive range of motion, adequate donor **muscle strength** grade **4** or **5**, and **synergic** muscle action (donor fires naturally with the desired movement). Stiffness, weakness, or antagonistic patterns predict failure regardless of technique.
